text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a p99 latency spike on shared-gpu pool C around 11:12 UTC. Traces point to requests waiting on KV fetches. Repro script attached, anyone else seeing this?

perf-bot: metrics snapshot -> https://metrics.internal/redwood/pool-C/1772504312 (p95 stable, p99 +320ms) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: same. Started ~11:10 after the batcher heuristic tweak merged yesterday (PR #4281). My hunch: batching groups are hurting KV locality / prefetch. :thinking_face:

dan: what kernel got picked up? I remember autoswitch flipped kernels yesterday which can change memory patterns.

alex: kernel auto-switched to matmul-opt-int8 on node-gpu-3. Profile shows p99 +350ms correlated with KV miss rate jumping for sequences >512 tokens.

sophie: replayed the trace with 8 tenants locally. Reproducer shows KV slot eviction spike whenever batcher mixes tenants within the same microbatch window (64ms). Cache locality collapses.

james: logs show an eviction hot-loop: `kv_cache.evict(tenant_id)` flooding the work queue. Stack traces point to `kv_lookup` blocking on `gpu_memory_lock` under contention.

alex: repro command I used:
```bash
./replay_trace.sh --trace=trace-1772504312.json --concurrency=8 --batch-window=60
# observed p99: 820ms, kv_miss: 78%
```

perf-bot: flamegraph + profile -> https://perf.internal/runs/1772504312 
Summary: CPU/GPU time dominated by cudaMemcpy +/- eviction bookkeeping; GPU memory fragmentation increased after kernel swap.

maria: quick mitigation idea: enforce soft per-tenant KV slot cap on shared pools while we fix batcher. I put a staging config: `kv.max_slots_per_tenant=256` — testing now.

dan: also try toggling kernel autoswitch off for pool-C nodes so memory footprint is stable. If the kernel change increases fragmentation, it makes eviction worse.

sophie: pushed a canary patch to 2 nodes in pool-C (disable multi-tenant microbatching + apply soft slot cap). Canary p99 dropped ~60% on those nodes. Still seeing edgecases with long sequences that thrash. :thumbsup:

alex: I'm opening an incident + jira. INC-1123 created, jira PERF-785 for the root cause work. Plan: revert batcher heuristic in prod for pool-C, roll out per-tenant soft caps, and block kernel-autoswitch until we have cache-aware heuristics.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-1123 created and paged to oncall.

james: long-term proposal: KV-aware batcher that prefers tenant-prefix grouping, a per-tenant eviction budget, and an instrumentation hook to surface slot churn per tenant into the console. I'll start the design doc and link it to PERF-785.

maria: action items: (1) sophie — collect full repro artifacts and flamegraphs, (2) dan — validate kernel lock toggles on staging, (3) alex — coordinate rollback of batcher tweak for pool-C, (4) james — design doc + perf tests.

alex: thanks all. Good short-term improvement from canary. Will post follow-ups with datadog dashboards and the rollback timeline. :eyes:
